incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT triggered: prod-runner-6 GPU OOM spike (prefill stage). Alert group: inference-prefill-oom. 10+ container restarts across 2 nodes in the last 5m. Paging on-call. https://alerts.redwood.example/alert/inf-prefill-2387654333

Sanjay: I'm on it. Root cause suspect: large prefill requests (long system prompts + long user history) causing KV/cache to blow memory during prefill. Will pull logs from the affected pods.

Emily: grabbing pod list now:
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=prod-runner -o wide | grep Running
prod-runner-6-5b7f6   1/1 Running 3 (3 restarts)   gpu-node-12   10.10.12.7
prod-runner-8-9c4d2   1/1 Running 1 (1 restart)   gpu-node-15   10.10.15.11
```

Emily: logs (last crash) from prod-runner-6: 
```
2026-03-15T02:12:44Z ERROR runtime: prefill failed for req_id=cli_9a7f: CUDA out of memory. tried to allocate 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 40.0 GiB total, 2.0 GiB free)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/runtime/prefill.py", line 214, in run_prefill
    kv_cache.store(prefix_tokens)
  File "/srv/runtime/kv_cache.py", line 89, in store
    buf = cuda_malloc(size)
RuntimeError: cuda runtime error (2): out of memory
```

Taylor: That stack looks like we're materializing the full prefix into the KV cache during prefill; large system prompts or full conversation history could blow the allocation. We've seen similar when a single tenant sends 200k-token context.

Maya: @Sanjay I'm taking incident lead. I'll page CS for potential customer impact. Can you confirm which requests were impacted and if there were any 500/connection reset responses?

Sanjay: pulling traces now. Filtering by req_id pattern and tenant tag. Early look: the bulk of errors from tenant "acme-telemetry" (tenant_id=acme-telemetry), ~120 requests in 3m where clients requested max_context ~196k tokens. Most of them failed in prefill with OOM and the client saw 502/GRPC CANCELLED.

Leo: noted. This tenant was testing long transcript ingestion. We should throttle them immediately. I can add a tenant-level rate limit and a per-request max token cap.

Taylor: Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Route this tenant to a smaller-context model variant (e.g., model-x-16k -> model-x-8k) to avoid large KV allocations.
2) Set an env override to cap prefill tokens (REDWOOD_PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=8192) and rollout to prod-runner; this will reject/trim dangerous requests.
3) Enable on-the-fly prefill streaming (stream into KV instead of materializing) - longer-term change.
4) Cordon problem node(s) and let workload reschedule to nodes with more free capacity (short-term but disruptive).

Maya: implement 1 and 2 now. I'll also notify CS that we are throttling the tenant and may be rejecting very large contexts. @pagerduty please escalate to the customer success channel.

pagerduty: Escalation posted to #customer-success: "Prod inference instability due to large-context prefill for tenant acme-telemetry. Temporary routing + caps applied. CS please reach out if customer-facing errors observed." :white_check_mark:

Emily: Applying env override to deployments:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/prod-runner REDWOOD_PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=8192 --record
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/prod-runner
```

Emily: Also pushed a route override: route.acme-telemetry -> model-x-8k (via routing service). Patch applied and warmed.

Sanjay: I'm watching the restart; rolling restart will bounce some connections but should reduce OOMs once env var is picked up.

incident-bot: Noted: config change event detected. 2 deployments restarted. Monitoring for new OOMs.

(5m pass)

Emily: After rollback/cap: prod-runner-6 restarts decreased from 3 in 5m to 0 in last 4m. Alert noise dropping. Current OOM count in last 10m: 1 (edge case).

Taylor: There's one stubborn session that still triggered a crash before route override finished. Logs show repeated attempts to prefill a >50k token single prompt. We should consider returning an explicit 413 (Payload Too Large) for requests >prefill cap instead of trying to process.

Maya: Agreed. For now, we are returning a 400 with a new error code PREFILL_TOO_LARGE for those requests to make it actionable for clients. @Sanjay can you add quick changelist to return that?

Sanjay: pushing a 2-line patch to runtime prefill handler to short-circuit when requested_prefill_tokens > env cap: 
```
if requested_prefill_tokens > int(os.getenv('REDWOOD_PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS', '999999')):
    return http_response(413, {"error":"PREFILL_TOO_LARGE", "message":"requested context exceeds supported limit"})
```

Sanjay: deploying canary to prod-runner-8 first.

Leo: For long-term: we should add per-tenant prefill quotas, streaming prefill, and a memory-aware guard on KV cache allocations. Also investigate whether KV cache retains allocations when prefill aborts (possible leak).

Taylor: I'll open two tickets: INF-2345 (prefill streaming + memory guards) and INF-2346 (tenant prefill quotas + routing safeguards). We need an owner for each.

Maya: Owner assignments: Taylor -> INF-2345, Leo -> INF-2346. Add expected timeline: quick guard within 2 weeks, full streaming in 6-8 weeks.

Sanjay: CS update draft: "We've identified that large prefill requests from your tenant exceeded our per-request memory guard and led to GPU OOMs for a subset of inference nodes. We've applied a temporary cap (8k tokens) and routed large requests to a smaller-context model. You may receive PREFILL_TOO_LARGE errors for extremely long contexts. Our engineering team is working on durable fixes." Thoughts?

Maya: fine. Send after we confirm no remaining 500s.

incident-bot: Alert status: degraded -> recovered (threshold). No active page.

Sanjay: Handing off to night on-call Taylor for follow-up and regression watch. Handoff notes:
- Actioned: env cap=8192, routing override for acme-telemetry -> model-x-8k, short-circuit returns 413 for >cap.
- Monitoring: watch OOM alerts, pod restart counts, 5xx rate for acme-telemetry.
- Follow-ups: INF-2345/Taylor (prefill streaming), INF-2346/Leo (tenant quotas), root cause deeper dive on KV cache leaks (Sanjay).

Taylor: Taking oncall. I'll keep alerting rules tightened: add tenant-specific anomaly rule for large-context spikes and add a runbook step to apply route override quickly.

Maya: Thanks team. CS notified. I'll close the page if no regressions in 1h. :thumbsup: 

Leo: note for postmortem: include exact memory allocation traces and tenant request characterization (token distribution). Also consider adding per-request prefill memory estimation before allocation.

Emily: I'll collect kube events and node-level dmesg for the postmortem.

Sanjay: tagging this thread for postmortem: /incident postmortem: GPU OOM - prefill long-context - 2387654333

Maya: closing page to on-call. Monitoring continues. :lock: 

(End of thread)
